# Repair a scientific finite-temperature workflow

This task contains a pinned snapshot of the open-source Spinach spin-dynamics
library and an offline scientific reproduction. A finite-temperature relaxation
experiment produces an unexpected result: a state calculated as thermal
equilibrium can drift under the corresponding relaxation dynamics, and
equivalent Liouville-space representations can disagree about the same
physical experiment.

Investigate the issue as a scientific-software problem. Read the supplied
scientific context, run the reproduction, and inspect the surrounding source
behavior before editing. Repair the implementation so that the physical
behavior of the workflow is restored without changing the public API.

The goal is one coherent repair, not a fixture-specific workaround. Preserve
the scientific meaning of the workflow outside the displayed experiment and
do not hard-code its inputs, dimensions, or reported categories.

Run the public reproduction with:

```bash
python reproduce.py
```

Keep generated files under `outputs/` and do not rely on network access,
MATLAB, or external data.
The supplied Spinach snapshot produces a scientifically inconsistent result in
a finite-temperature Liouville-space relaxation workflow. A calculated thermal
equilibrium state is not reliably stationary under the dynamics that should
preserve it, and equivalent representations can disagree about the same
physical experiment.

Inspect the supplied scientific context and source, run the public
reproduction, and repair the implementation. Preserve the public API and avoid
introducing assumptions tied to the displayed fixture, matrix dimensions, or

Run the offline smoke experiment from the task root:

```bash

```

The script constructs a small four-spin fluorine system using the normal
Spinach initialisation path. It then runs the actual finite-temperature
equilibrium calculation, relaxation assembly, both public thermalisation
routes, and a short relaxation-only propagation.

The printed report is symptom-oriented. It contains representation and method
labels, finite status, qualitative residual categories, a physical observable
consistency check, and two additional qualitative diagnostics for state
normalization and response consistency. Exact values, expected rates, and
implementation locations are not part of the public report. The pre-fix
snapshot is expected to expose scientific inconsistencies; the reproduction
process itself should remain repeatable and offline.

The command must run in the benchmark's GNU Octave image with network access

# Offline scientific context: finite-temperature spin dynamics

This document provides the scientific background needed to interpret the
offline reproduction. It is a neutral summary of the physical contracts of a
finite-temperature spin-dynamics calculation; it is not a repair recipe.

## 1. Density operators and Liouville space

Spin dynamics describes an ensemble state with a density operator `rho`. A
simulation may store that operator as a vector in Liouville space, where a
matrix acts as a generator:

```text
    d rho / dt = R rho
```

The entries of `rho` are coordinates in a chosen representation. They are not
individually observable physical quantities. A different representation can
use a different coordinate layout while describing the same experiment.

## 2. The two Liouville representations in this task

The supplied Spinach snapshot supports two relevant representations:

- a compact spherical-tensor representation, which can exploit spin
  symmetries;
- a full Zeeman-product representation, which stores the operator space in a
  vectorized matrix form.

The representations are expected to agree on physical observables after the
appropriate conversion, but raw coordinate vectors and raw matrix entries do
not have to match. Scientific agreement must therefore be assessed through the
represented state and its observables rather than by matching array entries.

## 3. Finite-temperature equilibrium

At nonzero temperature, equilibrium is the normalized Boltzmann state generated
by the Hamiltonian. In Liouville coordinates its exact values depend on the
Hamiltonian, temperature, and representation. The representation-independent
requirement is that a generator which is claimed to relax toward that state
must leave it unchanged:

```text
    R_thermal rho_eq = 0
```

This is the same idea as a fixed point in a numerical dynamical system: if the
system is initialized at equilibrium, a relaxation-only propagation must not
create a new signal or drift away from equilibrium.

## 4. Thermalisation methods

Spinach exposes two finite-temperature routes used by the historical
validation examples:

- the inhomogeneous-master-equation (IME) construction, which embeds a target
  equilibrium state into a homogeneous generator;
- the DiBari-Levitt construction, which transforms a relaxation generator with
  a finite-temperature Hamiltonian propagator.

They use different numerical constructions, but they describe the same
physical relaxation process when their assumptions hold. Agreement should be
judged through fixed-point behavior and observables, not by comparing matrix
entries across representations.

## 5. What the reproduction measures

The public experiment uses a small four-spin fluorine system with chemical
shifts and scalar couplings adapted from a bundled Spinach molecular example.
It constructs the system through the normal Spinach initialisation path and
then invokes the ordinary finite-temperature equilibrium, relaxation,
thermalisation, and propagation interfaces.

The report is deliberately symptom-oriented. It records whether the result is
finite, whether the computed equilibrium remains stationary, and whether a
physical readout changes during a short relaxation-only propagation. It does
not provide an exact numerical answer or identify an implementation location.

## 6. References

- Hogben et al., *Spinach - A software library for simulation of spin dynamics
  in large spin systems*, Journal of Magnetic Resonance 208 (2011),
  <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jmr.2010.11.008>.
- Levitt and Di Bari, *Steady State in Magnetic Resonance Pulse Experiments*,
  Physical Review Letters 69 (1992),
  <https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.69.3124>.
- Kuprov, *Defeating the Matrix*, Journal of Magnetic Resonance 306 (2019),
  <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jmr.2019.07.031>.
- Spinach documentation, <https://spindynamics.org/wiki/index.php?title=Main_Page>.

The links are provenance references only. The benchmark must run with network
access disabled using the files supplied in the task payload.

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path


TASK_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
FIXTURES = TASK_DIR / "fixtures" / "public"
SOURCE = TASK_DIR / "source"
OUTPUTS = TASK_DIR / "outputs"


def main() -> int:
    octave = os.environ.get("OCTAVE", "octave")
    if shutil.which(octave) is None:
        print("GNU Octave is required; use the science-bench-agent-octave image.")
        return 2

    compat = FIXTURES / "octave_compat"
    expression = (
        "addpath(genpath('" + str(SOURCE).replace("'", "''") + "'));"
        "addpath(genpath('" + str(FIXTURES).replace("'", "''") + "'));"
        "addpath('" + str(compat).replace("'", "''") + "');"
        "task015_public_case();"
    )
    completed = subprocess.run(
        [octave, "--no-gui", "--quiet", "--eval", expression],
        cwd=TASK_DIR,
        text=True,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
        check=False,
        timeout=240,
    )

    cases: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    for line in completed.stdout.splitlines():
        if not line.startswith("TASK015_CASE|"):
            continue
        fields = line.split("|")
        if len(fields) < 8:
            continue
        cases.append(
            {
                "formalism": fields[1],
                "method": fields[2],
                "dimension": int(fields[3]),
                "status": fields[4],
                "fixed_point": fields[5],
                "trajectory": fields[6],
                "observable": fields[7],
                "normalization": fields[8] if len(fields) > 8 else None,
                "response": fields[9] if len(fields) > 9 else None,
                "error": fields[10] if len(fields) > 10 else None,
            }
        )

    payload = {
        "schema_version": "0.2",
        "offline": True,
        "octave_return_code": completed.returncode,
        "cases": cases,
    }
    OUTPUTS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    (OUTPUTS / "public_reproduction_report.json").write_text(
        json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n", encoding="utf-8"
    )
    print(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
    # This command reports the scientific symptom; it is not a complete
    # correctness oracle for a candidate repair.
    if completed.returncode != 0 or not cases:
        print(completed.stdout)
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

Now I understand the structure. The error "R appears to be thermalized already." comes from `grumble` at line 83-84. It checks if `norm(R*unit,2) > 1e-10`. 

So for the zeeman-liouv formalism, `R*unit` is not small. The check is that the relaxation superoperator `R` should drive the system towards the zero state vector (i.e., `R*unit ≈ 0`). If `R*unit` is large, that means the relaxation superoperator already has a thermalization component (it's not purely damping to zero).

Wait, but the reproduction uses `inter.equilibrium='zero'` and `inter.relaxation={'damp'}`. So `R` from `relaxation(spin_system)` should drive toward zero. The issue must be with the unit state in the zeeman-liouv formalism.

Let me look at the `unit_state` function and the `relaxation` function. The check is `norm(R*unit,2) > 1e-10`. The unit state should be the equilibrium of the damping (zero-target) relaxation. So if `R*unit ≠ 0`, then either:

%
% Arguments:
%
%      L          -  Liouvillian or Hamiltonian to be used for 
%                    propagation; centre point piecewise-constant
%                    rule if one matrix is supplied, piecewise-
%                    linear rule if two matrices {left, right} 
%                    are supplied, piecewise-quadratic if three
%                    matrices {left, midpoint, right} are given.
%
%      rho        -  state vector or density matrix to be propagated
%
%      time_step  -  length of the time step to take
%

%       here - subspace, orthogonalisation, projection, etc., but in all

grumble(L,rho,time_step);

source/kernel/utilities/clean_up.m
% Array clean-up utility. Drops non-zero elements with magnitude below the
% user-specified tolerance and converts between sparse and full storage de-
% pending on the density of non-zeroes in the array. Syntax:
%
%                 A=clean_up(spin_system,A,nonzero_tol)
%
% Parameters:
%
%            A  - a numerical array or a cell array thereof
%
%   nonzero_tol - nonzero tolerance
%
% Outputs:
%
%            A  - cleaned-up array
%
% i.kuprov@soton.ac.uk
% alex_nevzorov@ncsu.edu
%
% <https://spindynamics.org/wiki/index.php?title=clean_up.m>

function A=clean_up(spin_system,A,nonzero_tol)

% Skip opium objects
if isa(A,'opium'), return; end

% Skip if disabled
if (nonzero_tol==0)||isnan(nonzero_tol), return; end

% Process cells recursively
if iscell(A)
    for n=1:numel(A)
        A{n}=clean_up(spin_system,A{n},nonzero_tol);
    end
    return
end

% Process polyadics recursively
if isa(A,'polyadic')
    for n=1:numel(A.prefix)
        A.prefix{n}=clean_up(spin_system,A.prefix{n},nonzero_tol);
    end
    for n=1:numel(A.suffix)
        A.suffix{n}=clean_up(spin_system,A.suffix{n},nonzero_tol);
    end
    for n=1:numel(A.cores)
        for k=1:numel(A.cores{n})
            A.cores{n}{k}=clean_up(spin_system,A.cores{n}{k},nonzero_tol);
        end
    end
    return
end
   
% Check consistency
grumble(A,nonzero_tol);

% Check if clean-up is allowed
if ~ismember('clean-up',spin_system.sys.disable)
    
    % Clean up the matrix
    A=nonzero_tol*round((1/nonzero_tol)*A);
    
    % A small non-zero matrix should always be full
    if issparse(A)&&(nnz(A)>0)&&...
       any(size(A)<spin_system.tols.small_matrix), A=full(A); end
    
    % A big sparse matrix with too many non-zeros should be full

import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path


TASK_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
FIXTURES = TASK_DIR / "fixtures" / "public"
SOURCE = TASK_DIR / "source"
OUTPUTS = TASK_DIR / "outputs"


def main() -> int:
    octave = os.environ.get("OCTAVE", "octave")
    if shutil.which(octave) is None:
        print("GNU Octave is required; use the science-bench-agent-octave image.")
        return 2

    compat = FIXTURES / "octave_compat"
    expression = (
        "addpath(genpath('" + str(SOURCE).replace("'", "''") + "'));"
        "addpath(genpath('" + str(FIXTURES).replace("'", "''") + "'));"
        "addpath('" + str(compat).replace("'", "''") + "');"
        "task015_public_case();"
    )
    completed = subprocess.run(
        [octave, "--no-gui", "--quiet", "--eval", expression],
        cwd=TASK_DIR,
        text=True,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
        check=False,
        timeout=240,
    )

    cases: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    for line in completed.stdout.splitlines():
        if not line.startswith("TASK015_CASE|"):
            continue
        fields = line.split("|")
        if len(fields) < 8:
            continue
        cases.append(
            {
                "formalism": fields[1],
                "method": fields[2],
                "dimension": int(fields[3]),
                "status": fields[4],
                "fixed_point": fields[5],
                "trajectory": fields[6],
                "observable": fields[7],
                "normalization": fields[8] if len(fields) > 8 else None,
                "response": fields[9] if len(fields) > 9 else None,
                "error": fields[10] if len(fields) > 10 else None,
            }
        )

    payload = {
        "schema_version": "0.2",
        "offline": True,
        "octave_return_code": completed.returncode,
        "cases": cases,
    }
    OUTPUTS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    (OUTPUTS / "public_reproduction_report.json").write_text(
        json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n", encoding="utf-8"
    )
    print(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
    # This command reports the scientific symptom; it is not a complete
    # correctness oracle for a candidate repair.
    if completed.returncode != 0 or not cases:
        print(completed.stdout)
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

% Modifies the relaxation superoperator to drive the system to the user-
% specified target state (inhomogeneous master equation formalism) or to
% the equilibrium state of the lab frame Hamiltonian at the temperature
% provided by the user (DiBari-Levitt formalism). Syntax:
%
%           R=thermalize(spin_system,R,HLSPS,T,rho_eq,method)
%
% Parameters:
%
%     R       - symmetric negative definite relaxation super-
%               operator that drives the system towards the
%               zero state vector; this may be obtained from
%               relaxation.m if inter.equilibrium is 'zero'
%
%     HLSPS   - lab frame Hamiltonian left side product super-
%               operator, available from hamiltonian.m (also
%               call orientation.m if necessary); this is not
%               required for IME formalism (pass empty array)
%
%     T       - absolute temperature, not required for the 
%               IME formalism (pass empty array)
%
%     rho_eq  - thermal equilibrium state, not required for 
%               the DiBari-Levitt formalism (pass empty array)
%
%     method  - 'dibari' for DiBari-Levitt thermalisation,
%               'IME' for the inhomogeneous master equation
%
% Outputs:
%
%     R       - thermalized relaxation superoperator
%
% Note: to work correctly, IME requires the population of the unit state 
%       in the state vector to be exactly 1. Spinach has no way of check-
%       ing or enforcing this requirement - take due care.
%
% Note: DiBari-Levitt method is computationally expensive, but tends to
%       work better than IME, particularly in exotic regimes.
%
% i.kuprov@soton.ac.uk
%
% <https://spindynamics.org/wiki/index.php?title=thermalize.m>

function R=thermalize(spin_system,R,HLSPS,T,rho_eq,method)

% Check consistency
grumble(spin_system,R,HLSPS,T,rho_eq,method);

% Get the unit state
unit=unit_state(spin_system);

% Choose the method
switch method
    
    case 'IME'
        
        % Apply IME correction
        R=R-kron(unit',R*rho_eq);
        
    case 'dibari'
        
        % Get the temperature factor
        beta=spin_system.tols.hbar/(spin_system.tols.kbol*T);

        % Modify the relaxation superoperator
        R=R*propagator(spin_system,HLSPS,1i*beta);
        
    otherwise
        
        % Complain and bomb out
        error('unknown thermalization method.');
        
end

end

% Consistency enforcement
function grumble(spin_system,R,HLSPS,T,rho_eq,method)
if (~isnumeric(R))||(size(R,1)~=size(R,2))
    error('R must be a square matrix.');
end
unit=unit_state(spin_system);
if norm(R*unit,2)>1e-10
    error('R appears to be thermalized already.');
end
if ~ischar(method)
    error('method must be a character string.');
end
if strcmp(method,'IME')
    if isempty(rho_eq)
        error('rho_eq cannot be empty for IME formalism.');
    end
    if (~isnumeric(rho_eq))||(~iscolumn(rho_eq))
        error('rho_eq must be a column vector.');
    end
end
if strcmp(method,'dibari')
    if isempty(HLSPS)
        error('HLSPS cannot be empty for DiBari-Levitt formalism.');
    end
    if (~isnumeric(HLSPS))||(size(HLSPS,1)~=size(HLSPS,2))
        error('HLSPS must be a square matrix.');
    end
    if norm(HLSPS*unit,2)<1e-8
        error('HLSPS appears to be a commutation superoperator.');
    end
    if isempty(T)
        error('T cannot be empty for DiBari-Levitt formalism.');
    end
    if (~isnumeric(T))||(~isreal(T))||(~isscalar(T))||(T<=0)
        error('T must be a positive real scalar.');
    end
end
end

% Returns the unit state vector or matrix in the current formalism
% and basis. Syntax:
%
%                     rho=unit_state(spin_system)
%
% Parameters:
%
%    spin_system  - Spinach data object containing basis 
%                   information (call basis.m first)
%
% Outputs:
%
%    rho          - vector or matrix representation of
%                   the unit state 
%
% i.kuprov@soton.ac.uk
% d.savostyanov@soton.ac.uk
%
% <https://spindynamics.org/wiki/index.php?title=unit_state.m>

function rho=unit_state(spin_system)

% Check consistency
grumble(spin_system);

% Decide how to proceed
switch spin_system.bas.formalism
    
    case 'sphten-liouv'
        
        % Unit population of T(0,0) state
        rho=sparse(1,1,1,size(spin_system.bas.basis,1),1);
        
    case 'zeeman-liouv'
        
        % Normalized stretched unit matrix
        rho=speye(prod(spin_system.comp.mults));
        rho=rho(:); rho=rho/norm(rho,2);
        
    case 'zeeman-hilb'
        
        % Sparse unit matrix
        rho=speye(prod(spin_system.comp.mults));
        
    otherwise
        
        % Complain and bomb out
        error('unknown formalism specification.');
        
end

end

% Consistency enforcement

if (~isfield(spin_system,'bas'))||(~isfield(spin_system.bas,'formalism'))

end
end

%    Q            -  irreducible components of the anisotropic part

%                    fying the system orientation relative to the in-

%                    only isotropic part of the Hamiltonian is used.
%

%

===
% Returns a unit operator in the current formalism and basis. The
% operator has dimension equal to the basis size in sphten-liouv
% formalism, the dimension equal to the product of all spin multi-
% plicities in zeeman-hilb formalism, and the dimension of square
% of the product of all spin multiplicities in zeeman-liouv forma-
% lism. Syntax:
%
%                      A=unit_oper(spin_system)
%
% Parameters:
%
%    spin_system  - Spinach data object containing basis 
%                   information (call basis.m first)
%
% Outputs:
%
%    A            - a sparse unit matrix of appropriate
%                   dimension 
% 
% i.kuprov@soton.ac.uk
% d.savostyanov@soton.ac.uk
%
% <https://spindynamics.org/wiki/index.php?title=unit_oper.m>

function A=unit_oper(spin_system)

% Check consistency
grumble(spin_system);

% Decide how to proceed
switch spin_system.bas.formalism
    
    case 'sphten-liouv'
        
        % Unit matrix
        A=speye(size(spin_system.bas.basis,1));
        
    case 'zeeman-liouv'
        
        % Unit matrix
        A=speye(prod(spin_system.comp.mults.^2));
        
    case 'zeeman-hilb'
        
        % Unit matrix
        A=speye(prod(spin_system.comp.mults));
        
    otherwise
        
        % Complain and bomb out
        error('unknown formalism specification.');
        
end

end

% Consistency enforcement
function grumble(spin_system)
if (~isfield(spin_system,'bas'))||(~isfield(spin_system.bas,'formalism'))
    error('the spin_system object does not contain the required information.');
end
end
